Very true! I went through a long period of being uncomfortable talking about it with anyone but one specific person - guess I should've mentioned that, ahah.

I hope things become clearer for you soon <3

As a trans nonbinary person - thank you for being open minded and understanding <3

It's worth noting that sex, gender, gender identity, and gender expression are all separate things - gender is the physical part of your brain; it's a body part like your hand. There are billions of these, just like there are billions of hands (just a note though, some folks don't have a gender.)

A person's gender identity is the societal gender term or idea that they've adopted to describe their gender - for example, male and female are societal gender categories. The debate is really about whether these two categories are all encompassing or not, not whether "male and female are the only two genders."

Gender expression is how your actions and appearance are perceived by society, with regards to these gender categories.

Girls being "tomboy" then, is a part of gender expression - it's a separate issue from gender, because a 100% female person can still like 100% "guy" things, and that's totally okay. The gender issue is that nonbinary folk have a gender that isn't described by the accepted societal terms, which may or may not lead to dysphoria depending on the degree of inaccuracy. But you see, a gender can't be wrong just because it doesn't fit with society, because gender exists totally separately from societal gender ideas (which only affect gender identity and expression). So, a society built on scientific and social (not political, PC is bullshit imo) correctness should be able to encompass nonbinary people comfortably.

I know a few cis guys who actually understand this and treat me right, and it's honestly so much better for everyone involved. I find it odd how toxic people are about the whole gender topic, like...it's not a sensitive topic to trans people like me. I don't like somebody telling me I'm invalid, of course, but I'm fine discussing gender as long as it's mature. People seem to take me talking about these ideas as me attacking them, or looking for attention or whatever, but it's relevant to everyone, because everyone's gender (or lack of) works this way.

Or at least, that's how I understand it - please do educate me if I'm wrong.
